picks.excerpt: NVIDIA makes the case for open, downloadable world models in Omniverse — models teams can inspect, fine-tune and run on their own infrastructure to build simulated 3D worlds. The same world-model stack now being pitched at games and virtual production, framed as an openness argument rather than a demo reel.
picks.rationale: Open, self-hostable world models are the most concrete change to how 3D/level teams can prototype worlds — a real release, not commentary.

picks.excerpt: A long-form report on how generative AI is reshaping the Skyrim modding scene — from AI-voiced followers to slop uploads — and why mod host sites are struggling to build tagging and disclosure systems that keep the community's trust. Modders, players and site operators describe a transparency problem that existing UGC moderation tools were never designed for.
picks.rationale: Freshest deep report on AI disclosure inside a live UGC platform — directly informs how any creator community writes its own provenance rules.

picks.excerpt: Three veteran game localizers explain how to work with loc teams — and push back on the claim that they can simply be replaced by generative AI or machine translation. A practical look at where LLM translation actually breaks in games: context, culturalization, and the hand-off with design.
picks.rationale: Maps exactly where LLM translation fails in production and how design should hand off to loc — actionable tomorrow.

picks.excerpt: AniShort folds scripting, storyboards, character management, AI video generation, editing and rendering into a single browser-based pipeline. It is an argument that the win from generative AI is not the clip generator but the unified authoring workflow around it.
picks.rationale: A shipped tool that moves the value from clip generation to the whole authoring pipeline — a workflow pattern teams can copy.

picks.excerpt: With no new GTA 6 trailer, AI-generated fake gameplay and trailers are racking up millions of views across TikTok and Instagram. Generative video is now filling the vacuum in a game's marketing narrative — a real problem for how studios control their own visual identity pre-launch.
picks.rationale: Shows generative video hijacking a product's pre-launch visual identity — a brand-control problem every marketing/design lead now owns.

dropped_as_within_pool_duplicate.reason: Same event as the Rock Paper Shotgun Nexus Mods tagging-policy piece; kept the stronger single article, then dropped both in favour of the fresher RPS modding-transparency feature to avoid two near-identical mod-disclosure cards.
